fixes_after_first_look: drowning: dunk/hold a person in water, or hold a head down, when water and distress words co-occur
assault: explicit attacker twisting/yanking a limb; injury lexicon adds popped/snapped/deformed, 'cracked' needs a body part
arson: up to 6 words between the pour/soak verb and the accelerant

missing: strong absence words (missing/disappeared/vanished) need no extra cue for a child; weak departures (drove off, got on a bus) need a condition and a search/time cue for an adult; 'missing' uses a deny-list of objects (a tooth, recess, the bus...); twins/kiddos; 'nobody has seen her', 'the coach hasn't seen her', 'door unlocked', 'never on the bus', 'dog came home alone' cues; police/ems wording is not a resolution for missing-person reports; horseplay words (giggling, laughing) exclude
